Welcome to John Donne Primary School, a diverse and vibrant school in the heart of Peckham. We appreciate you taking the time to find out about us and our school.
John Donne is an exciting, creative and dynamic school where our focus is to give all children every opportunity to become successful, confident, curious and happy learners who will become future leaders and innovators. pageCache.text:
Headteacher's Welcome
Welcome to John Donne Primary School, a diverse and vibrant school in the heart of Peckham. We appreciate you taking the time to find out about us and our school.
John Donne is an exciting, creative and dynamic school where our focus is to give all children every opportunity to become successful, confident, curious and happy learners who will become future leaders and innovators. Our broad and aspirational curriculum is designed to support our children to achieve well academically as well as building the skills that will empower them spiritually, morally, socially and culturally to respond to a rapidly changing world.
We are hugely proud of our school and we hope that you take this opportunity to explore our website to find out more about what John Donne can offer. If you would like to see for yourself what makes John Donne such a special place, please contact the school office to arrange a visit.
Jo Rooney Headteacher

pageCache.text:
Our Vision, Mission and Values
Our Vision
To be happy, curious and successful members of our local and global communities, we know that the children of John Donne will need to not only achieve highly in reading, writing and mathematics but also thrive in creativity, the arts, their passions and beyond. Our aim is that every child leaves John Donne with a strong sense of self and of what makes them special.
Our Mission
To improve on our previous best.
To develop self-discipline and a positive self-image.
Our values
Our core values guide all that we do at John Donne for children and for our staff. They express how we work together to make sure we all achieve our very best both academically and personally.

Clubs
John Donne offers a wide range of school provisions.
We feel that these clubs help the children explore their interests and help them develop communication skills outside of the normal school day.
Ultimate Sports Club (USC) Breakfast Club
The breakfast club runs from 7:45am to 8:45am daily in the lower hall.
Children come through the school office and into the school hall to be admitted.
A breakfast of: cereal (Weetabix or Cornflakes), bagels and milk and fresh fruit is provided between 7:45am and 8:30am.
(Children must arrive between 7:45am and 8:00am to be served breakfast).
From 8:30 to 8:40 children are provided with both indoor and outdoor activities.
Whilst attending Breakfast Club, normal school rules apply and children will be expected to follow them.
If you need any further information about Breakfast Club or to enquire about availability of spaces, Ricardo Gordon on 074 6397 8692 or email info@ultimatesportsclub.co.uk to check availability.
Ultimate Sports Club (USC) After School Club
USC After School Club is run as an external activity club. Every day the children are offered different activities like gymnastics, dance, arts and crafts, cooking and multisport. These are not compulsory for the children; they can enjoy free play if they wish. The goal of the club is to offer a fun and safe environment for the children to enjoy and give them an opportunity to try new sports and activities. The after school club runs from 3:15pm until 6:00pm. Please contact USC for pricing information.
There are limited spaces in the club therefore, if you would like your child to attend please contact Ricardo Gordon on 074 6397 8692 or email info@ultimatesportsclub.co.uk to check availability.

We are a vibrant and diverse two form entry primary school located in the heart of Peckham. We would like to warmly invite all prospective parents to come and get a taste of what school life is like at John Donne. Please call the office to arrange a school tour on 0207 639 0594.
What makes John Donne a special place to learn?
Pupil Admission Number (PAN)
The school has an admission number of 60 for entry in Year Reception.
The school will accordingly admit this number of pupils if they are sufficient applications. Where fewer applicants than the published admission number(s) for the relevant year group are received, the Academy Trust will offer places at the school to all those who have applied.

Appeals are being managed by Bexley Council on behalf of the school.
Appeal application forms can be obtained from the school office by emailing office@jdacademy.org.uk
Nursery Admissions
Nursery Admissions
John Donne Primary School offer a free full day nursery provision. All nursery children aged 3 to 4 years are entitled to 15 hours free early education and childcare by the Government.
At John Donne, our nursery provision will operate using a 2.5 day attendance model for children accessing their 15 funded hours, alongside full-time provision for children eligible for 30 funded hours. It will also be possible for families to top-up hours beyond the funded entitlement for a fee.
The opening times for our Nursery are 8:45am until 3:15pm.
Nursery Admissions Criteria
John Donne Primary School is an academy school and we welcome children of every faith and from every background.
We are committed to include all children, able-bodied or disabled, gifted or with special needs. We will adapt our school where possible to meet with any child’s special needs. If you would like to see a copy of our accessibility plan please ask the school office.
We follow the admissions procedure agreed by the Southwark Admissions Forum.
Over-subscription Criteria for Nursery
In the event that there are more applications than there are places available, places will be allocated in the following order of priority:
(i) Children in public care (Looked-After Children) and children who were previously looked after but ceased to be so because they were adopted (or became subject to a child arrangements order or special guardianship order)
(ii) Children with siblings who are already on roll at the school and will still be on roll at their date of entry
(iii) Children with exceptional medical, social or psychological needs, where it is agreed by the Governing Body and the headteacher that these can best be addressed at the Academy
(iv) Children of permanent staff members who work at least three days per week
(v) Children living nearest to the school as measured by a straight line from the child’s home to the main school gate
How to Apply
Nursery Admissions
Applications for Nursery is made directly through the school. You can apply for your child to be added to our waiting list after they turn 2 either by email at admissions@jdacademy.org.uk or you can obtain an application form here.
Reception Admissions
Application for Reception is made by completing Southwark's on-line application form available here.

pageCache.pageTitle: John Donne Primary School - School Meals
pageCache.text:
School Meals
At John Donne School, we are proud to have an in-house catering team. Our catering team is lead by Mr Simpson, who is a qualified chef with over 20 years experience in the catering industry.
Our menu offers varied and flexible food choices for our children. All of the meals meet nutritional standards set out by the government. Fresh fruit, salad, bread and drinking water are always available.
Please click on the attachment below to see the weekly menu. For further information, please contact the school office.
FREE school meals
Southwark offers children in Nursery as well as Years 3, 4, 5 and 6 a free school meal as part of their Healthy Free School Meals scheme. The Government offer Reception to Year 2 pupils a free school meal as part of their Universal Free School Meals programme. Both programmes are designed to help tackle obesity and deprivation in the borough and nationally, as well as to ensure children are fed well at school, do better in their lessons and have improved general health and wellbeing.
All Parents and Carers, will be asked to complete a form for a Free School Meal regardless of their child's meal option.
Healthy packed lunch ideas
Lunch boxes don't need to contain just a sandwich and a packet of crisps. Ensuring the meal contains fruit and/or vegetables, a good helping of starchy carbohydrates and some dairy products will result in a nutritionally balanced lunch.
Healthy options

pageCache.pageTitle: John Donne Primary School - SEND and Inclusion
pageCache.text:
SEND and Inclusion
Inclusion
At John Donne Primary School, we believe that inclusion should be at the heart of everything that we do.
SEND
We consider it essential that the curriculum on offer to all our pupils is presented in a supportive and stimulating atmosphere, which values each child and encourages them to achieve the full potential. This encompasses the four main areas of SEND:
Communication and interaction
Cognition and learning
Social, mental and emotional health
Sensory and/or physical
EAL
As a diverse community school, we celebrate and value all of the children in our school, including those learning English as an additional language. We aim to provide visual learning opportunities in all lessons and differentiate learning to meet the needs of our pupils.
Wider Pastoral Team
We also understand that a range of factors can affect a child’s personal development and attitude towards school and learning. Our staff work alongside our wider pastoral team, parents, carers and external agencies to help offer a range of programmes and support networks to help and encourage children experiencing emotional barriers to their learning.

Governance
Welcome to the Local Committee
John Donne Primary School is delighted to be part of the Nexus Education Schools Trust (NEST), and although we work very closely with them, the day to day governance of our school is carried out by the Local Committee.
The key responsibilities of the Local Committee are as follows:
To operate effectively, the Local Committee appoints representatives who bring a wide range of knowledge and experience. The Local Committee consists of the Headteacher, Community representatives, Parent representatives and Staff representatives.
If you wish to contact any members of our Local Committee please email office@jdacademy.org.uk or telephone the school office on 0207 639 0594.
